subject: A third reactive table, based on two previous

messages.author: ed5b3bf6bf97b7b8
messages.subject: A third reactive table, based on two previous
parts:
Im trying Shiny and building a simple app to choose different values from two datasets, and the compare these values. See the app so far at : 

http://spark.rstudio.com/energidk/lasse/ 

(It takes a little time to load the data) 

The top table are future values, and the lower table is historical values. I would like a third table under does two, that can do simple calculations based on the day you choose. For example: 

I choose 2 days ahead, which means that in the box:  "Number of days to view, max 14:" is set equal to 2. Now I choose 7 historical days to compare with. 

Now I would like a third reactive table under these two, that simply does a percentage calculation, so: 
   
          Columns....
Row 1: day 2 values / day 1 historical
Row 2: day 2 values / day 2 historical
Row 3: day 2 values / day 3 historical... etc. 

My Shiny code so far: 

ui.R

library(shiny)

# Define UI for dataset viewer application
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  
  # Application title
  headerPanel("Germany Balance"),
  
  # Sidebar with controls to select a dataset and specify the number
  # of observations to view
  sidebarPanel(
    selectInput("dataset", "Choose Number of Days Ahead:", 
                choices = c("Base", "Peak", "Off-Peak")),
    
    numericInput("obs", "Number of days to view, max 14:", 7)
    
  ,
    # Slider
    selectInput("datahis", "Choose Number of Historical Days:", 
                choices = c("Base", "Peak", "Off-Peak")),
    
    numericInput("obshis", "Number of days to view:", 7)
),
  
  # Show a summary of the dataset and an HTML table with the requested
  # number of observations
  mainPanel(
    
    tableOutput("view"),
    tableOutput("hisview")
  )
))

server.R

# Server
library(shiny)
library(plyr)

# Define server logic required to summarize and view the selected dataset
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  
  # Return the requested dataset
  datasetInput <- reactive({
    switch(input$dataset,
           "Base" = base,
           "Peak" = peak,
           "Off-Peak" = offpeak)
  })
    
  # Show the first "n" observations
  output$view <- renderTable({
    head(datasetInput(), n = input$obs)
  })
  
  datahisInput <- reactive({
    switch(input$datahis,
           "Base" = h_base,
           "Peak" = h_peak,
           "Off-Peak" = h_offpeak)
  })
  
  # Show the first "n" observations
  output$hisview <- renderTable({
    head(datahisInput(), n = input$obshis)
  })
})

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: A third reactive table, based on two previous
parts:
So obviously, you'll need a third tableOutput and third output$xxx <- renderTable().

You can't reuse values that are calculated inside renderTable. But you can reuse reactives. So in this case, you can use datasetInput() and datahisInput() in your new renderTable. If head(datasetInput(), input$obs) is an oversimplification of what you're doing and you're actually doing more complicated processing inside the renderTable, just move that logic out into a separate reactive and reuse the reactive.
